qwen_same_evidence.note: Correctly identifies numerical dispersion and improved front localization with refinement, but does not explain front spreading or computational cost. The claim that refinement makes arrival later than reality contradicts convergence toward the correct solution in KB1.

agent.note: Identifies numerical dispersion and improved localization, but incorrectly asserts that front speed increases proportionally with grid count. KB1 does not support that relation. Front spreading and refinement cost are absent.

qwen_closed_book.note: Correctly links coarse grids to numerical dispersion and says refinement can mitigate the problem, but does not explain spreading across cells or computational cost. It incorrectly attributes numerical dispersion to inadequate representation of geological structure and property changes; dispersion also occurs in homogeneous displacement.

openai_same_evidence.note: Accurately explains spreading across cells, apparent early breakthrough, and reduction of dispersion with refinement. KB1–KB3 support the cited mechanisms. Additional computational cost is not mentioned.

openai_closed_book.note: Correctly explains numerical front spreading and early low-water-cut detection, with reasonable qualifications about other discretization effects. Recommends refinement tests but omits the computational-cost tradeoff.
